newsitem.title: USA: US West debt garners better bids, Raytheon steady.
newsitem.headline: US West debt garners better bids, Raytheon steady.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds held firm as demand for the $4.1 billion US West Capital Funding bonds pushed those prices higher, while Raytheon Co debt was spared further erosion post two downgrades, dealers said.

Raytheon's outstanding issues were quoted little changed on Friday, despite the company's assumption of $4.4 billion in debt in its proposed $9.5 billion acquisition of General Motor Corp's Hughes Aircraft defense subsidiary.
The debt had widened about five basis points on Thursday after the announcement and subsequent rating downgrades by Standard & Poor's and Moody's Investors Service.

Traders on Friday stressed overall trade was slow, but that Moody's decision to keep its rating of Raytheon debt within the "A" range helped prevent further erosion. Standard & Poor's cut long-term debt to BBB from BBB-plus and Moody's cut its rating to A3 from A1.
Raytheon's 6-1/2 percent 10-year notes were quoted at 60 bid, 55 offer late Friday.

Raytheon Co Chief Financial Officer Peter D'Angelo on Friday said the company expects to pay down about $7.0 billion of debt over a seven-year period. The CFO also said Raytheon will issue $4.5 billion in two-, 10- and 30-year debt.
US West Capital Funding's deal captured the spotlight again on Friday, meanwhile, with all tranches of the $4.1 billion deal tightening about three basis points, according to several traders.

New issues on Friday included $220 million in five- and 10-year debt from American Health Properties Inc via lead manager Goldman, Sachs & Co. Five-year debt was priced as 7.05s to yield 80 basis points over Treasuries and 10-year debt was priced to yield 105 basis points over.
Turning to high-yield issues, traders reported a typically quiet Friday session with prices little changed on the whole.

Merisel Inc's 12-1/2 percent senior notes dropped almost 10 points on Friday, however, following a run-up of equal proportions on Thursday, one trader said. Merisel on Thursday said it expected to report a return to profitability in the fourth quarter of 1996.
New high-yield issues featured $250 million 10-year senior notes from Century Communications Corp, priced as 8-7/8s to yield 255 basis points over Treasuries via a J.P. Morgan Securities syndicate.
Elsewhere, Loomis Fargo & Co issued $85 million senior subordinated notes due 2004 in the private placement market at par to yield 10.00 percent via a Lehman Brothers group.
The following deals also priced, according to MCM CorporateWatch.
-- Brazil's Aracruz Celulose issued $120 million in five-year Eurobonds in the private placement market to yield 255 basis points over Treasuries via Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.
-- Imperial Credit Industries Inc issued $200 million 10-year senior notes in the private placement market to yield 9.875 percent via a Lehman Brothers syndicate.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association recommended a 1400 EST/1900 GMT close for the U.S. fixed-income markets on Friday and a full close on Monday in observance of the Martin Luther King Day holiday.
The benchmark 30-year T-bond closed up 1/32 at 95-26/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
